faulty: 1-nearest-neighbour regression (Euclidean distance on X standardised with the training mean and sd) under 5-fold cross-validation (fold = i mod 5) on all 600 rows as given; pooled mean absolute error of the held-out predictions; skill = 1 - MAE(model)/MAE(training-fold mean predictor); holds iff skill >= 0.10.
fixed: Rows with an identical X vector (standardised distance < 1e-8) are reduced to the first of each group (later rows dropped) before the same 5-fold cross-validation on the remaining rows; skill >= 0.10.
estimand: Faulty: skill on held-out rows many of which have an identical record in the fitting rows. Fixed: skill for new distinct entries.
model_family: 1-nearest-neighbour regression, Euclidean distance on standardised measurements; chosen because it returns the target of an identical record exactly, which is how duplicated records enter, and because it is numpy-only.
sizes_note: Source states none. 600 x 8 = 4,800 values; the check is a 600 x 600 distance matrix per fold (milliseconds). Dependence on sample size or duplicate share: not stated. Mean-absolute-error skill (family other) is used because it separates the worlds at a realistic duplicate share (about 0.36 or more of the rows), whereas R-squared with one neighbour would need about 0.6.
exploited_structure: Repeated records of the same entry among the rows, so that a held-out row has an identical row among the fitting rows.

def stat(d):
    X = np.asarray(d["X"], dtype=float)
    X = (X - X.mean(axis=0)) / (X.std(axis=0) + 1e-12)
    sq = (X ** 2).sum(axis=1)
    D = np.sqrt(np.maximum(sq[:, None] + sq[None, :] - 2.0 * (X @ X.T), 0.0))
    n = D.shape[0]
    med = np.median(D[~np.eye(n, dtype=bool)])
    np.fill_diagonal(D, np.inf)
    return float(np.mean(D.min(axis=1) < 0.1 * med))
